subject: Extending the MCMC chain - solved already?

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: Extending the MCMC chain - solved already?
parts:
Hello,

I am starting a new project now and considering to use nimble; so I am checking if there is any update about the biggest nimble setback I found in my past project. Unlike in JAGS and others, it was not possible in nimble to save the model and later extend the MCMC chains of the saved model when more iterations are needed. It was only possible to extend the MCMC chain within the same R session, but once that one ended, the model is saved and later restored, it no longer worked. (So especially in parallel processing, it was virtually impossible to get the extend)

Thanks for the update!

Tomas

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Extending the MCMC chain - solved already?
parts:
Other developers might have more to add to this - regarding the future ability to save models - but as of now: you are correct, you cannot save a model, or MCMC.  You can, however, in a new R session build an identical model and MCMC, and begin execution from exactly where the last MCMC left off - both in terms of the values of the parameters being sampled, and also the internal adaptation and tuning of the MCMC.  If you also take the extra step of saving the old R RNG seed, and restoring it to that value, this approach is equivalent (in terms of the samples generated) to having run the original chain longer.

Would that be helpful to you, for the time being?

Daniel

messages.author: 9c2c0c89a3d22b1b
messages.subject: Re: Extending the MCMC chain - solved already?
parts:
Hi Tomas,

Just wanted to double what Daniel wrote. In my case I save all variates as Monitor2, with a thinning equal to the number of iterations, so that only their last values are saved (or more exactly I assign to Monitor2 the variates that are not already monitored in Monitor1). These values can be used as initial values in a new chain that is set up identically to the first otherwise. In my case I do this in case I want to run the (finished) chain for longer, after checking some diagnostics.

Cheers,
Luca

Thanks!

Tomas

messages.author: 9c2c0c89a3d22b1b
messages.subject: Re: Extending the MCMC chain - solved already?
parts: > but isn't there more to be saved, for the MCMC chains to continue exactly where they left off?

From what I've noticed, not: just the hyperparameters and the random seed. I tested this by (1) running a chain this way (final states of all nodes saved), then restarting R, recompiling, and continue the chain using those final states as initial values; (2) running the initial chain for longer. The overlapping parts are exactly identical.

It may well be that it only works in my case though (Dirichlet mixture of product kernels). Daniel or Chris know best!

Maybe you may try the same test and see if it works for you too.

Cheers,
Luca

messages.author: 9c2c0c89a3d22b1b
messages.subject: Re: Extending the MCMC chain - solved already?
parts: > The overlapping parts are exactly identical.

That was really badly expressed. I meant the chains are exactly identical, even the later parts that have been obtained using the two different procedures.

Sorry and cheers,
Luca

Daniel
